Title: if I were in the V:tES design team ...

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
[card idea article]

no Archon Investigation or similar cheese! Check this one out:

Outpost

Master, Location (_non-unique_), 0 pool cost

When you sustain pool loss due to being successfully bled,
tap Outpost to designate an untapped minion you control to
enter combat with the acting minion. Does not prevent
the pool loss. Your minion becomes tapped and is considered
the blocking minion in the combat. No strike: combat ends may
be played in the combat. If the acting minion survives the
combat, another Outpost (and another untapped minion) may be
used in succession.

Illustration: armed-and-dangerous guy in watch-tower, looking
meaningfully at sneaky guy walking along street below.

Flavor Text: "It is dangerous to mess with he who is always
alert ... " - annonymous

Of course, this has to be a common card.

--
"Live Life with Heart."

Alan Kwan kw...@cs.cornell.edu

In article <49iq6p$j...@bert.compusmart.ab.ca> Errol T <etre...@compusmart.ab.ca> writes:
>
>I can tell you didn't think this one through very well Alan,This so
>called card idea is exactly like Archon investigation except you get to
>beat the crap out of him instead of just buring him,and you do it without
>spending 3 pool,unless they come of the vampire in the form of Additional
>strikes.

Big difference. You need to build an entire combat deck to
support it, and it doesn't work against bruise-and-bleed.
It's more like a permanent Bum's Rush against S&B, but you
don't fight until you've /taken/ a bleed, which may well be
more than 3 pool (especially if he /knows/ that he'll lose
his vampire to your Outpost ...) You need to keep a vampire
untapped to fight him. And, in most cases, you torporize,
but don't /burn/.

This card would be close to Archon Investigation, if your
predator plays a straight S&B deck with absolutely no combat
elements in the deck. But "Bloodhunt" or "Archon" can pretty
much do the same, or more.

I didn't say "Acting minion may not play any strikes in this
combat", did I?

Messages.Author: Nicole Janine Purvis
Messages.Body:
Thomas R Wylie (aa...@cats.ucsc.edu) wrote:

: Alan's card is a Majesty hoser, and a narrow one at that, since it can only
: be used if you have already been bled. If it is a bleed hoser, then why does
: it let the bleed through?
Cards can be hosers by punishing certain actions or clans, etc., not
necessarily just by preventing them.

: Why does it prevent Combat Ends?
: And I'm surprised that nobody has pointed out that the
: backstory is inconsistent: outposts are supposed to keep people out, not let
: you jump them after they've already gotten through your defense.
I assumed that the Outpost had already been breached [the minion had
enough stealth to get in and bleed without being stopped], but that the
bleed was discovered afterwards before the acting minion could escape,
and thus the outpost manners would kick the acting minion's rear end on
the way out. Since the minion is already inside the outpost, trying to
escape out of a defended area once discovered wouldn't be feasible. I
assumed that was why Combat Ends couldn't be used.

: This is not to say that Alan's card is a terrible card. But whether or not
: you think AI is munchkinized, and whether or not you think Alan's card is
: munchkinized, it is not a bleed hoser.
Varying opinions. Granted, it's not as much of a hoser as AI [which I
still don't know what it does, except that it burns a bleeding vampire
without letting him do the bleed damage?], but I guess that goes with the
arguments that AI is not balanced enough.

Errol: Think about these facts with AI:
The vampire is burned for 3 pool.
The bleed is unsuccessful (no Edge, no damage, just 3 pool loss)
If a person has all Jyhad backs, why worry?
To remove a vampire normally requires combat, a vote, or a
return of the investment (a la Golconda). There is a chance of failure.
To hose votes we have: Beaureacratic Overload (DS card, all PA
cost 1 Pool).
To hose combat we have majesty.
To hose bleeds we have: DESTROY the Vampire.
Is there a comparison to the power of AI anywhere? Please, give
examples.
Your Contention about Alan's being unbalancing.
The vampire CAN be destroyed, given a card combo in hand and
given the Bleeder doesn't have a defense. Who Bleeds well? Ventrue
(defense of Majesty, Fortitude, and Thoughts Betrayed (DS card: No combat
cards playable by opponent), Toreador (Celerity, Majesty), Brujah
(Celerity, Potence, Majesty), Malkavian (Thoughts Betrayed,
Disguised/Concealed Weapon). They have a CHANCE of making it.
They succeed in the Bleed (get the Edge, even if the vamp croaks).

Alan's works (though is in my mind complicated). AI doesn't.

Tom: Read the above. The card hoses bleeds by getting combat to the
bleedee.
Why this matters:
Every combat able clan can defend against bleeds.
Bleed Bounce and Counter, and Intercept are not the only
bleed defenses. It is a bleed hoser.

Opinion: AI is only viable if the bleed succeeds.

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Alan's card is a Majesty hoser, and a narrow one at that, since it can only
be used if you have already been bled. If it is a bleed hoser, then why does
it let the bleed through? Why is it preventing Combat Ends? It's not all
that different from a Haven Uncovered that prevented Combat Ends instead of
granting a maneuver. And I'm surprised that nobody has pointed out that the
backstory is inconsistent: outposts are supposed to keep people out, not let
you jump them after they've already gotten through your defense.

This is not to say that Alan's card is a terrible card. But whether or not
you think AI is munchkinized, and whether or not you think Alan's card is
munchkinized, it is not a bleed hoser.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.
